decisions.reason: Underground load-haul-dump loaders fit our core underground machinery, safety and service capabilities, so even with weak recent website evidence we are more likely to learn and improve than exit.
Underground mining dump trucks also build on closely related vehicle, mining-application and after-sales knowledge, which supports continued refinement rather than withdrawal.

A construction site dumper is related to our transport and construction equipment know-how but sits in a broader and less distinctive market, so we keep it while recognizing a meaningful exit risk if learning does not translate into sales.

An inclined furniture lift is comparatively distant from our strongest underground and heavy-duty application knowledge, so our absorptive capacity to improve and scale it is weaker and redeployment of resources is more attractive.
An inclined building material lift is closer to our construction-site and lifting competences than the furniture-lift products, giving us a reasonable base to adapt and support it commercially.

Although truck integration is within our technical reach, the truck-mounted inclined furniture lift still targets a less related customer segment and support model, making discontinuation more likely than sustained development.
